body.p: Claims 1-20 were pending in this application, and claims 1, 11, and 16 were the independent claims. Claims 11-20 are withdrawn. Claims 1-10 are rejected.

In this response, claims 1, 4-6 are amended. Claim 2 is canceled without prejudice. Support for the amendment can be found throughout the specification, for example, in paragraphs 75-83 and FIGS. 3A, 3B.
Applicant's representative Fredrick Tsang, Reg. No. 68,680 conducted a telephonic

interview with Examiner Tu on May 3rd, 2023. During the interview, pending claims 1-20 and the rejections to those claims under 35 U.S.C. §§ 102 and 103 were discussed. While no specific agreement was reached during the interview, Applicant thanks the Examiner for taking the time to conduct the interview.
Claims 4-5 are objected to because of informalities. The claims have been amended to correct the informalities. Therefore, the objections should be withdrawn.
Claims 1 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as anticipated by Niederkrom et al. '277 (US Pub No. 2014/0366277). In view of the following, these rejections should be withdrawn.

An embodiment discloses an air-permeable bedding system comprising a microclimate fabric layer and an air-permeable capacitive layer. The air-permeable capacitive layer comprises two air-permeable substrates, each carrying a set of electrically conductive pathways. As recited in the amended claims, the two sets of electrically conductive pathways are separated by an air-

permeable dielectric layer. The air-permeable dielectric layer defines a horizontal air pathway that allows for airflow horizontally between the two sets of pathways. The two air-permeable substrates also position the two sets of electrically conductive pathways to define vertical air pathways that allow airflow to pass vertically through gaps in a sensor grid.
Niederkrom does not disclose the following elements of amended Claim 1:
The air-permeable dielectric layer defines a horizontal air pathway
allowing for airflow horizontally between the two sets of electrically
conductive pathways.
or:
The two air-permeable substrates securely position the two sets of electrically conductive pathways to cross over each other, forming
capacitors at intersection points, the intersection points defining a sensor grid, and wherein the sensor grid comprises a plurality of gaps that define
a plurality of vertical air pathways such that airflow passes vertically
through the gaps in the sensor grid and horizontally through the air- permeable dielectric layer.
Specifically, Neiderkrom does not disclose a horizontal air pathway (airflow through a dielectric layer) or a vertical air pathway (airflow through gaps in a sensor grid).

Instead, Neiderkrom discloses airflow through a spacer material, a layer of material with one of its two surfaces proximal to a pressure sensing mat. Neiderkrom at [0009]. In paragraph 27, Neiderkrom teaches that air may flow through the spacer material, "cover sheet 100 comprises an air mover 140 configured to provide air flow through spacer material 110." In paragraph 33, Neiderkrom further teaches that, upon use, "moisture vapor may be transferred from a person (and the surrounding air) through vapor permeable material 120 and into air pockets within spacer material 110."

Neiderkrom does not disclose a horizontal air pathway or teach that air may flow through a dielectric layer. In paragraph 30, Neiderkrom merely teaches that a dielectric may be "compressible," and that "during use, compressible dielectric 127 may be compressed and a

thickness 117 of pressure-sensing mat 125 reduced." Thus, Neiderkrom does not disclose "the air-permeable dielectric layer defines a horizontal air pathway allowing for airflow horizontally between the two sets of electrically conductive pathways" as recited in amended claim 1.

Additionally, Neiderkrom does not disclose a vertical air pathway or teach that air may flow through gaps in a sensor grid. Neiderkrom merely teaches that "electrical conductors 126 form a grid across pressure-sensing mat 125." Neiderkrom at [0029]. Thus, Neiderkrom does not disclose "a plurality of vertical air pathways such that airflow passes vertically through gaps in the sensor grid and vertically through the air-permeable dielectric layer" as recited in amended claim 1.
Moreover, Neiderkrom does not disclose the following element of amended claim 1:
The two air-permeable substrates securely position the two sets of
electrically conductive pathways to cross over each other forming a
capacitor at one or more intersection points, the one or more intersection
points defining a sensor grid.

Instead, Neiderkrom merely discloses a capacitance "of the electrical conductors" and that electrical power may create capacitance in the grid, "electrical power is provided to pressure-sensing mat 125, which creates a capacitance in the grid of electrical conductors 126." Neiderkrom at [0030].
Accordingly, reconsideration and withdrawal of the art rejections are respectfully requested.

Based on the foregoing, the application is in condition for allowance of all claims, and a Notice of Allowance is respectfully requested. If the examiner believes for any reason direct contact would help advance the prosecution of this case to allowance, the examiner is encouraged to telephone the undersigned at the number given below.

If extensions of time are necessary to prevent abandonment of this application, then such extensions of time are hereby petitioned under 37 CFR 1.136(a), and any fees required therefore are hereby authorized to be charged to our Deposit Account 19-2555.
Respectfully submitted,
